solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Knocking back a lager, floppy maybe, do yourself an injury

indicators.note: knocking back a drink means downing it, and 'back' says the letters run the other way

blocks.note: A plus PILS, short for Pilsner, a pale lager
a floppy is a kind of computer disc; 'maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a lager and somehow ends up hurting themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A PILS read backwards gives SLIP A; add DISC for SLIP A DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping a disc is a common back injury, a prolapsed spinal disc, so it is something you might do to yourself.

clue.text: Dwarf tending to ejaculate involuntarily?

blocks.note: first meaning: one of Snow White's seven dwarfs
second meaning: prone to sneezing, since ejaculate also means to exclaim or expel suddenly

explanation.walkthrough: The rude reading of 'ejaculate' is the joke; its older sense is to blurt or expel suddenly, which is what a sneeze does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sneezy keeps sneezing, an involuntary sudden expulsion of air, and Sneezy is also the dwarf's name.

clue.text: Olive might ... bugger off

blocks.note: first meaning: an olive might be filled with pimento or anchovy
second meaning: a rude dismissal telling someone to go away

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis lets the phrase finish the first sentence, 'Olive might get stuffed', and then stand alone as the insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Get stuffed is a British slang brush-off equivalent to go away, and literally what happens to a filled olive.

clue.text: Bastards turning over the old lady – disgrace!

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: gits are contemptible people, a British insult
one's old lady is one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: Some louts knock over somebody's mother, a shameful act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is slang for mother. Git is a mild British term of abuse for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: (& 20ac.) Spring tip and ring joined makes you hung like a horse?

blocks.note: a spring is a source of water, a well
the tip of something is its end
O is ring-shaped
to be wed is to be joined in marriage

explanation.surface: A crude boast: a few things combined will give you impressive genitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(& 20ac.)' tag says the answer runs on into 20 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Well endowed is a euphemism for having a large penis, which is what the horse comparison crudely implies.

clue.text: One who makes prick large and acne-riddled, right?

indicators.note: riddled suggests something shot through and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the four letters rearranged
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A smutty riddle about a spotty man and the size of his member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prick' looks like the rude noun, but it is the verb: a lancer pricks something open.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or puncture, as with a boil, so a lancer is someone who pricks.

clue.text: Patriotic figure's way to get stuffed: storing energy

indicators.note: storing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to gorge is to eat until stuffed
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: England's patron saint is shown filling up on a feast to keep his strength up.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits after the first letter of GORGE, making GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George is the patron saint of England, the emblem of English patriotism.

clue.text: Embarrassed to snog such a reactionary type?

blocks.note: embarrassed people go red
to neck is to kiss passionately; snog is British slang for the same

explanation.surface: Someone would be mortified to be caught kissing a bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: A redneck is a derogatory American term for a rural, politically conservative white working-class man.

clue.text: Amphetamine too "up" for her?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read rising from the bottom

blocks.note: E is slang for ecstasy, an amphetamine-type drug
too means also, as AND does

explanation.surface: Asks whether a woman is too high on speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' also suggests being high on drugs, hiding its job of turning round only the word for 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's first name, so the pronoun stands for a female person.

clue.text: Vat raised by party about to balls up

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps the other
raised in a down clue means lifted so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: Lab is short for the British Labour Party
to balls something up is to blunder, to err

explanation.surface: A political party lifts a vat while making a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls up' reads like a rude image of something raised, but it is the British slang verb for botching, here meaning to make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel is a large cylindrical container, the same thing as a vat or cask.

clue.text: Smooth party's unscrupulous recruiters

blocks.note: to press clothes is to smooth them
a party of people is a gang

explanation.surface: A slick political party is accused of shady recruitment tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang forcibly enlisted men into the navy, a notoriously ruthless method of recruitment.

clue.text: The terrorist leader finally stuffed!

blocks.note: first meaning: the final part of the al-Qaeda leader Osama bin ... name
second meaning: heavily loaded or full

explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' points to the last word of the terrorist's full name, not to a last letter. 'Finally stuffed' also reads as a gloat about his death.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or weighed down, so a full, stuffed container is laden.

clue.text: (& 14ac./21dn.) Question from self-important type pissed off by apparent lack of recognition?

annotation.answer: DO YOU REALISE WHO I AM

definitions.text: Question from self-important type pissed off by apparent lack of recognition?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pompous person asks something

blocks.clueFragment: pissed off by apparent lack of recognition?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the indignant line a celebrity snaps when not given special treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the famous huffy question of a VIP who has not been recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stock indignant demand of someone who thinks their status entitles them to deference.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Loose talk of unemployed having crack? Piss off!

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: out of work is idle
to have a crack at something is to have a go
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The jobless chatter about having a go, then are told to get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle gossip is careless rumour and chit-chat, the meaning of loose talk.

clue.text: Enjoying Nancy's delights? Not knackered, he won't, maybe

indicators.note: knackered means broken or worn out, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
maybe hints that the words could be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man too lively to be tired out refuses to stay home from some saucy fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a city in north-east France, so its delights are those of a town; the name also hints at something racier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the town means out enjoying a place's nightlife and entertainments.

clue.text: Too much booze is bad, trapping Barack finally

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows
trapping means holding something caught inside

blocks.note: bad in the moral sense is sinful
the last letter of Barack

explanation.surface: A moral warning about heavy drinking, with Barack Obama caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes in after the first letter of SINFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is British slang for as much alcohol as one can hold, enough to get drunk.

clue.text: Trendy TV series: Having it off with a Sloth

indicators.note: off implies something knocked out of place, so those two letters swap round

blocks.note: fashionable things are in
ER was a long-running US hospital drama
the two letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy TV show apparently features someone having sex with a sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having it off' is British slang for sex, but here 'it' is the fodder and 'off' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a vice means laziness, and inertia is a sluggish disinclination to move or act.

clue.text: Grease strip put on by an old sailor in shower?

definitions.text: put on by an old sailor in shower?

blocks.note: oil is a grease or lubricant
to skin something is to strip its outer layer

explanation.surface: A greasy striptease performed by an old seaman in the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'shower' is rain, not a bathroom; the definition describes the garment by who wears it and when.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof coat of oiled cloth worn by fishermen and sailors in wet weather.

clue.text: Lots of twits ignoring Brown's end

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the word before it
ignoring means leaving something out of account

blocks.note: a noodle is a silly person
the last letter of Brown

explanation.surface: Plenty of idiots are snubbing Gordon Brown at the end of his premiership.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first N of NOODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a large amount, as in oodles of cash.

clue.text: see 5dn.
see 13ac.
Grit produces split round middle of pants

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter
round means going all the way around something else

blocks.note: a gash is a cut or split
the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A tear appearing round the crotch of someone's underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants are underwear, which is the joke; 'Grit' is a verb, as in gritting your teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together, the same action as gritting them.

clue.text: Frottage is, truthfully, somewhat unfair to the elderly

indicators.note: somewhat means only partly, so just a run of letters from the words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Frottage, all of is and the start of truthfully

explanation.surface: Someone admits that sexual rubbing really does exclude older people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination by age, typically against older people, so an ageist attitude is unfair to them.

clue.text: Extra! Posh getting end away!

indicators.note: getting its end away means the final letter is sent off and dropped

blocks.note: plush means luxurious, posh

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline: a posh person has had sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply removes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an additional benefit, something extra.

clue.text: Pissed but looking brilliant?

blocks.note: first meaning: drunk, British slang
second meaning: illuminated, shining

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone drunk yet looking great; pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit up is slang for drunk and also literally means illuminated, so brightly shining.

clue.text: Drink up second crap drink

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to sip is to drink
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Finish your drink, then have a second, awful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Piss is slang for weak or bad beer, as in 'this lager is piss'.

clue.text: Maidens possibly restrained – went mad with the retail therapy?

definitions.text: went mad with the retail therapy?

blocks.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so maidens are examples of overs
pent, as in pent-up, means held in

explanation.surface: Some young women who had held back finally splurged at the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maidens' look like young women, but they are cricket overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail therapy is shopping to cheer oneself up; going mad with it means spending too much money.

clue.text: Windsor, for one, gets sailor in a lather

blocks.note: soap is what makes a lather; the S is the possessive of 'a lather's'
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A royal Windsor finds a sailor all worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor in a lather' is read as a lather's sailor, SOAP'S TAR. Barbara Windsor played Peggy Mitchell in the BBC soap EastEnders.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Windsor is a well-known British actress from television soap opera, so an example of a soap star.

clue.text: "Tool positioning aid" looked a puzzle

blocks.note: a jig holds work and guides a tool into the right position
saw is the past tense of see

explanation.surface: A quoted product name puzzles someone who reads it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks keep 'Tool positioning aid' together as one description, and 'Tool' tempts as a definition since a jigsaw is also a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces to be reassembled.
